newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore oil products supported by firmer crude.
newsitem.headline: Singapore oil products supported by firmer crude.

text.p: The Singapore fuel oil and gas oil market were steady to shade softer on Monday despite poor regional demand and high supplies as the market looked to the crude market and colder weather in the west for support, traders said.
A major offered 30,000-tonnes of gas oil loading in end January at $30.80 a barrel on a free-on-board Singapore basis, up slightly from Friday's $30.65 traded level.

Traders said the market remains fundamentally weak due to sharply lower Chinese demand for February cargoes with Indonesia still not seen in the market for its February requirement on high regional availabilties.
Supplies were seen available from South Korea, Japan and Singapore for late January and February lifting, traders said.
Traders said the upcoming sale tender from Taiwan where up to three 225,000-250,000 barrels cargoes maybe sold is another bearish factor.
Sentiment was also dampened by India's decision to buy only 135,000-tonnes in its February supplementary tender against an initial market expectation of 200,000-tonnes.
Jet fuel also fell on renewed selling interest due to poor demand from North Asia for the winter. A trader offered 100,000 barrels for $32.55 a barrel fob Singapore.
The fuel oil market saw some support from firmer crude prices despite little spot demand from China and several cargoes headed to the region from the MidEast and the U.S.
A major offered 20,000-tonne loading in February 3-7 at $117.50 per tonne, down 50 cents from Friday's offer price.
